name: VAmPI, the vulnerable REST API
excludeWhy: README.md is the answer source (it lists the nine vulnerability classes); the Postman collection is an exploit walkthrough. The OpenAPI spec stays: it is the app's routing table.
docSource: README.md section 'List of Vulnerabilities' (nine classes, no locations) and its 'vulnerable' switch: each class is guarded by a vuln flag and the other branch is the project's own safe version

items.description: SQL injection: username concatenated into a query
Any logged-in user can change another user's password
Any user can read any book's secret by title (broken object level authorization)
Registration accepts an admin flag from the request body
Unauthenticated debug endpoint returns every user including passwords
items.docRef: README.md: Excessive Data Exposure through debug endpoint

items.description: Login errors tell whether the username exists and whether the password was wrong
Email validation regex with nested quantifiers (catastrophic backtracking)
Login and other endpoints have no rate limiting or resource limits
items.docRef: README.md: Lack of Resources & Rate Limiting

items.description: JWTs are signed with the constant secret 'random'
items.docRef: README.md: JWT authentication bypass via weak signing key

decoys.description: vuln=0 branch: book lookup restricted to the owner
vuln=0 branch: registration ignores the admin flag
vuln=0 branch: one generic login error
vuln=0 branch: password update only for the token's own user

notCovered: Plaintext password storage and comparison (models/user_model.py, api_views/users.py): real, not in the README list, and not switched by the vulnerable flag
debug=True and host 0.0.0.0 in app.py, and Flask debugger exposure
No authentication on /users/v1/{username} and the user list: by design in the README flow
The README says some things stay vulnerable with the flag off (the debug endpoint), so a finding in a decoy branch about plaintext passwords is partly right; decoy hits are reported and read by hand
Anything else. A finding there is 'unmatched'; the 10 highest severity unmatched findings per app were classified by hand
